combat_progression.rationale: Full credit for substantive combat and progression implementation.
evidence: public/app.js defines drone, zig, and tank enemies with distinct health, speed, value, and color at lines 167-188.
public/app.js implements difficulty-based spawn rates, enemy firing, projectile collisions, contact damage, score awards, lives, and game-over at lines 199-291.
automated.json records successful firing, enemy spawning, and a game-over adapter state with score 7317.

visual_design.rationale: The screenshots show a cohesive, polished neon arcade visual system across desktop and mobile, with clear hierarchy and active-state feedback.
evidence: desktop-before.png visibly shows the cyan/pink neon palette, strong display typography, framed mission and leaderboard panels, glow treatment, grid, and branded hierarchy.
desktop-after.png visibly shows RUNNING status, SOUND OFF feedback, animated-looking star/grid canvas treatment, glowing player craft, HUD, and populated leaderboard.
mobile.png visibly shows responsive single-column layout, readable headline, compact panels, and a five-button touch control pad without horizontal overflow.
public/style.css and public/app.js implement the responsive layout, gradients, scanlines, grid, stars, glows, particles, enemy/player artwork, screen shake, and reduced-motion CSS.

resilience_accessibility.rationale: Loading, empty, error/retry, validation, and non-blocking network-failure states are implemented, with strong basic semantic labeling.
evidence: public/app.js:444-505 implements loading, empty, error, retry, and playable-on-sync-failure leaderboard states.
public/app.js:508-552 validates names and scores, disables submission during requests, and restores the button after failures.

public/index.html provides labels, aria-live regions, aria-pressed mute state, canvas/lives labels, and labeled touch buttons; automated.json reports six labeled elements and no console or page errors.

data_security.rationale: The checked-in migration applies RLS, tight grants, database validation, and minimum public leaderboard operations; the retained remote test confirms the deployed anon read/insert path.
evidence: supabase/migrations/202608060001_neon_barrage.sql creates the leaderboard constraints, enables RLS, grants anon only SELECT and column-limited INSERT, and defines no update/delete policy.
public/config.js contains only the Supabase URL and anon key; no service-role or privileged browser credential is present.
automated.json/browser-evaluator.log records remote leaderboard GET 200, POST 201, subsequent GET 200 requests and persisted=true.

engineering_quality.rationale: Build, lint, tests, lockfile, and source separation are solid; one point is withheld for shallow automated coverage and an advertised but unimplemented pause shortcut.
evidence: build.log and build.exit-code show a successful deterministic dist build with exit code 0.
lint.log/lint.exit-code show both JavaScript files pass node --check with exit code 0.

test.log shows four passing tests covering name/score validation, collision behavior, and score formatting; package-lock.json is committed and public/game-logic.js separates reusable logic from the main loop.
public/index.html advertises ESC PAUSE, while public/app.js keyboard handling covers arrows/WASD/Space but has no Escape branch; the tests do not exercise the full game loop or lifecycle.

reproducibility.rationale: The source tree provides a complete handoff beyond the result artifact.
evidence: README.md documents local setup, controls, architecture, security decisions, testing/build commands, migration usage, and Cloudflare deployment.
supabase/migrations/202608060001_neon_barrage.sql, scripts/build.mjs, wrangler.toml, package.json, and package-lock.json provide reproducible schema, build, deployment, and verification inputs.
source-manifest.txt retains both source and built dist artifacts, and build.log records the successful build output.

summary: Manual award: 45/46. The implementation is strong across gameplay, visuals, resilience, Supabase security, and handoff; the only deduction is for limited full-loop test coverage and the unimplemented ESC pause hint.
